subject: Acme trial - procurement & billing readiness / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Acme trial - recap, procurement questions & next steps

Hi Alex / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to see the usage during the pilot and agree on the success criteria. Quick recap and a couple of procurement/billing questions so we can land the commercial path:

Recap (from call):
- Pilot scope: 3 prod routes + 1 batch embedding job; target 10M tokens/week peak.
- Success criteria: 95% of responses under 750ms median latency, <2% regression vs baseline, and conversion of 3 pilot apps to production by end of trial.
- Timeline: trial ends 2026-11-12; proposed start of billing 2026-11-15 if criteria met.

Procurement questions (so we can finalize legal/payment flow):
1) Will Acme be able to issue a PO (net 30) or prefer to pay by corporate card?
2) Do you require a company-to-company SOW or is the standard Redwood order form sufficient?
3) Are you interested in procuring via the AWS Marketplace listing (we can provide an invoice through the marketplace)?

I attached a draft SOW and a pricing worksheet showing PO vs card vs marketplace pricing differences.

Next steps:
- Please confirm procurement preference and any internal PO routing deadlines.
- If PO: can you share the required billing/PO contact and sample PO timeline?
- If marketplace: confirm whether finance needs partner/vendor IDs.

I'll loop in Rishi (SE) on the integration checklist and Dev for any implementation blockers.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: ACME_SOW_draft.pdf, Redwood_pricing_worksheet.xlsx

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 16:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme trial - recap, procurement questions & next steps

Marissa —

Thanks for the summary and the docs. Quick answers from our side:
- Procurement prefers PO (net 30) for anything > $50k. For smaller pilots they might allow a card.
- We generally need an SOW plus an order form; the SOW should reference our standard data handling addendum (I attached the template in a separate thread earlier).
- We could do Marketplace but finance prefers direct company-to-company for contractual reasons.

A couple of follow-ups: can you provide an estimated invoice schedule if we start billing on 11/15? Also, our legal will want to review the SOW — can we get a clean PDF?

I'll loop procurement distribution for PO timeline.

Alex
Director, Product Integrations | Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com

Hi team —

Thanks Alex — noted PO preference. Quick answers and proposed path:
- If Acme issues a PO (net 30): Redwood can accept PO + signed order form. Invoice cadence: monthly in arrears. If billing starts 2026-11-15, first invoice would cover 11/15-12/14 and be due net 30.
- If you need the SOW as a clean PDF, attached (ACME_SOW_draft.pdf). We're happy to accept your DPA/data handling addendum; Rishi will coordinate any technical language.
- Marketplace: pricing is similar but procurement/legal teams often prefer direct contracting as Alex mentioned. If you want the marketplace route we can provide the listing link and marketplace invoice flow.

Trial-to-paid conversion checklist we recommend (to avoid surprises):
- Confirm success criteria pass (we'll run the evaluation and share results by 11/10).
- Confirm start date for billing (you suggested 11/15; confirm if that's workable).
- Confirm PO issuance timeline and billing contact (we need PO number before first invoice).

Action items:
- Alex: confirm if 11/15 start date is OK and share procurement contact and timeline.
- Procurement: share sample PO and any required attachment checklist.
- Rishi/Dev: I've cc'd you — can you prepare a short integration readiness note and the latency/throughput report we promised?

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out so Acme can move to production.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: ACME_SOW_draft.pdf

Marissa / Alex —

Thanks. Procurement prefers the PO route. Our timeline: procurement approvals typically take 7-10 business days once we have a clean SOW + pricing worksheet and the billing contact. We need the following to start the PO:
- Clean SOW PDF (received).
- Final pricing worksheet (please confirm the unit and any overage rates).
- Billing contact, invoice email, and remit-to details.

If all is provided today we can target PO issuance by 2026-10-30. Also confirm whether the PO should reference your AWS Marketplace listing or Redwood legal entity (Redwood Inference, Inc.).

Regards,
Procurement Coordinator | Acme Corp
procurement@acme.com

Great — thanks for the timeline. Quick confirmations:
- Final pricing worksheet attached (Redwood_pricing_worksheet.xlsx) — pricing rows show card, PO, and marketplace parity; note: marketplace includes ~2% fee in the list price.
- Billing contact: finance-invoices@redwood.ai
- Remit-to: Redwood Inference, Inc., 123 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94105 (we'll include full remit details on invoice).
- Please reference Redwood Inference, Inc. (not marketplace) on the PO; we'll provide marketplace reference only if you decide to route via AWS later.

Start date: 2026-11-15 is fine from our side — we'll switch billing on that date if success criteria are met and your PO is in place. If PO issuance slips, we can provisionally start on card and convert later, but we prefer to finalize PO to avoid invoice/collection work.

Next: Rishi — can you please attach the latency/throughput report and a short integration readiness checklist to this thread? I'll update the HubSpot deal and flag legal to expect the SOW review.
